newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Small U.S. company has huge Caspian oil find.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Small U.S. company has huge Caspian oil find.

text.p: American International Petroleum Corp. said Thursday that estimates of potential recoverable reserves in its Caspian Sea oil find had risen to 1.1 billion barrels of oil.
The tiny oil exploration company said there could be more to come from as-yet-unexplored areas in its holdings in the Caspian Sea.
The Caspian is usually reserved for the giants of the oil world such as Exxon Corp., Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Brtish Petroleum Plc and Chevron Corp., as well as major Russian firms such as LUKoil.
Total reserves in the Caspian are estimated up to 200 billion barrels of oil, almost as much as those found in top exporter Saudi Arabia.
American said that it had access to existing pipeline infrastructure to ship any commercial production out of its discoveries.

Its holdings are 125 miles southeast of one of the largest discoveries in the region, the massive Tengiz field, which is operated by Chevron, a joint venture between LUKoil and ARCO, Mobil Corp. and the Republic of Kazakhstan.
That field has some 6 billion barrels of reserves.
It also borders a field operated by France's Elf Aquitaine in the Azerbaijan sector of the Caspian, which has potential reserves of around 375 million barrels.

There was some controversy earlier this year when the Kazakh government started awarding exploration licenses to smaller oil companies, including American and an Indonesian company called Central Asia Petroleum.
According to analysts, smaller companies often lack the capital and the political connections to develop such substantial reserves.
Its partners in the venture are MED Shipping, a consortium of U.S. and Kazakh business people who have been working in the region since 1993.
On the financial front, the company believes it will also have the necessary firepower.
"There have already been drilling partners which have been speaking to American and they are household names," said a company spokesman.

American International, which sold its Latin American and African operations to buy a 70 percent interest in the 4.7 millon-acre Caspian concession, said it had tested seven areas called geological structures.

However, potential for more reserves existed in nine additional geological structures in the east of its concession, with one, a 23-mile geological structure offering strong indications from seismic testing.
"The company believes that this structure, whose potential reserves are not yet estimated, could provide the largest potential deposit in the area," the company said in a statement.
American International Petroleum's stock rose 31 cents to 94 cents on Nasdaq.
